prompt.context: Alpha Capital is a private equity firm that is looking to buy a high-end male fashion retail chain named BNG. This is a private retail chain that was started in California 20 years ago. Alpha Capital is looking to see a 25% ROI in 3 years. They want us to help them decide whether to buy BNG and assess BNG's economic growth in 3 years.
prompt.question: Should Alpha Capital acquire BNG? What is the maximum price Alpha Capital should pay for BNG, and what factors drive BNG's growth prospects?

clarifying_info.q: How many retail outlets does BNG have, and where are they located?
clarifying_info.a: BNG has 10 retail outlets, all in California.

clarifying_info.q: What is BNG's current annual revenue?

clarifying_info.a: BNG sells men's jeans, shirts, and shoes, all sold only in their own boutiques to control the high-end image.
All clothing is manufactured in the US.

clarifying_info.q: What is BNG's current profit margin?
clarifying_info.a: The chain currently experiences 20% profit margin.
The owner will sell the chain for a one-time payment.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected revenue growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: Growth will be 10% for the next 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of capital?

exhibits.title: Demand Curves by Product Category
exhibits.shows: Demand curves for BNG's product categories (belts/shoes vs. shirts/pants), illustrating how quantity demanded changes with price
exhibits.data: Two distinct curve shapes are shown: a linear demand curve for shirts/pants, and a kinked (double-kinked) demand curve for belts/shoes with a sharp drop in demand at particular price points

framework: High-end Male Fashion Market: Total Addressable Market, Market Share of Competitors, Expected 3-year Growth, Competitive Dynamics
BNG's Profitability: By product mix, by customer sub-segment, by channel (online vs. retail), relative to competitors, brand/customer awareness
Alpha Capital Perspective: Retail experience, potential portfolio synergies, operational improvements
Macroeconomic conditions and industry growth rate
Consumer perceptions: size and growth of target demographic, potential to expand target market
Sales channels: potential to expand into new points of sale
Product mix: expansion of product line (accessories, lower end)
Operations: management team strengths and incentives, efficiency and outsourcing potential

questions.prompt: What factors would you look at to assess BNG's prospects for growth?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers: macroeconomic conditions, industry size and growth rate, competitive landscape, consumer perceptions and target demographic size/growth, pricing optimization potential, sales channel expansion, product mix expansion, brand awareness outside California, operations/management quality and incentive alignment, and efficiency/outsourcing potential.

questions.prompt: The owner of BNG is willing to sell the chain for a one-time payment. The chain currently experiences 20% profit and will earn $60 million next year. What factors should Alpha Capital look at to determine the maximum price to pay for BNG?
questions.guidance: Key factors: expected growth rate, industry comparables, macroeconomic considerations. Candidate should ask about growth rate, cost of capital, and time horizon. With 10% annual growth for 3 years and no cost of capital, total profits over 3 years drive the maximum price, discounted to achieve the 25% ROI hurdle.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum amount Alpha Capital would be willing to pay for BNG?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a 3-year profit projection using 20% margin on $60M revenue growing at 10%/year. Sum total profits then back-solve for price that yields 25% ROI.

math.setup: Revenue year 0 = $60M, profit margin = 20%, growth = 10%/year for 3 years. Profit each year = revenue * 20%. Total profits = sum of years 1-3. Maximum price = Total profits / 1.25 (to achieve 25% ROI).
steps: Year 1 profit: $60M * 1.10 * 20% = $66M * 20% = $13.2M... (Note: casebook uses $60M * 20% = $12.0M for Year 1, implying revenue figure given is already next-year revenue)
math.answer: Maximum price Alpha Capital should pay is $31.7 million.

questions.prompt: BNG's 10 stores have been experiencing dramatically different revenue. What do you think are the causes for this variability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should distinguish factors that vary by location (valid drivers) from factors that are consistent across all stores (not drivers). Store size, product selection, and in-store promotions/signage are consistent across all 10 stores, so candidate should focus on: store location demographics, foot traffic type (mall vs. standalone), proximity to competitors, local marketing efforts, proximity to supply chain, quality and experience of store management, and incentive practices for store staff.

questions.prompt: What are some drivers of growth for BNG?
questions.guidance: External drivers: macroeconomic conditions, competitive pressures, fashion trends. Internal drivers: products sold (variety, quality), sales channel selection (store locations), marketing effectiveness, operational effectiveness (production costs, distribution methods).

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What is your immediate reaction? What can BNG do to improve profits based on this exhibit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that belts/shoes have a kinked (double-kinked) demand curve while shirts/pants have a linear demand curve. BNG is in the inelastic portion for belts/shoes — they should raise prices there. For shirts/pants, BNG is in the elastic portion — lowering prices may drive volume but profitability depends on cost structure. For the kinks in the belts/shoes curve, these represent competitor price points (high-end and low-end competitive lines).

math.setup: Using index prices where current price=1 and current volume=1 (revenue=1). For belts/shoes (inelastic): raise price to 1.20, volume falls to only 0.9. For shirts/pants (elastic): lower price to 0.80, volume rises to 1.8.
steps: Belts/shoes after price increase: 1.20 * 0.9 = 1.08 (8% revenue increase, plus variable cost savings from lower volume)
Shirts/pants after price decrease: 0.80 * 1.8 = 1.44 (44% revenue increase, but profitability depends on variable cost structure)
math.answer: Raising belts/shoes price to $1.20 (index) increases revenue by at least 8% and also reduces variable costs. The kinks represent competitors' price points — competitors likely have both a high-end and low-end line of belts/shoes.

questions.prompt: BNG is considering opening 14 new stores. What factors are most important for the CEO to consider?
questions.guidance: Open-ended; a strong answer draws from throughout the case: store location selection (demographics matching target consumer, foot traffic, proximity to competitors), human capital (hiring/training quality management and staff, consistent incentive structures), supply chain scaling, brand awareness expansion outside California, capital requirements and financing, and operational consistency across new locations.

recommendation: Alpha Capital should consider acquiring BNG if the purchase price is at or below $31.7 million, which is the maximum price to achieve the required 25% ROI over 3 years based on 10% annual growth and 20% profit margins.
BNG has clear levers for profit improvement: raising prices on inelastic product lines (belts/shoes) and potential geographic expansion beyond California's 10 current stores.
risks: Revenue growth may not sustain 10% annually if macroeconomic conditions deteriorate or competitive pressure intensifies.
Store-level revenue variability suggests operational or management quality issues that may be difficult to fix at scale.
Opening 14 new stores requires significant capital and management bandwidth; execution risk is high.
BNG's California-only presence concentrates geographic risk.
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on store-level financials to understand the root causes of revenue variability across the 10 locations.
Validate the 10% growth rate assumption with market data on the high-end male fashion segment.
Assess management team quality and whether current incentive structures can scale.
Develop a site-selection framework for the 14 new stores, prioritizing demographics and competitive density.
Negotiate purchase price at or below $31.7 million.
